summary: Muvux Orthopedics, LLC (the firm's client and the buyer) is acquiring the cervical and lumbar interbody fusion implant business of Pisen Spine Technologies, Inc. under an Asset Purchase Agreement signed September 15, 2026. The purchase price is $68,000,000: $54,000,000 in cash at Closing and a $14,000,000 subordinated Seller Note issued by Muvux to Pisen. The form of Seller Note is attached as Exhibit B and will be dated the Closing Date. The folder holds the APA, the earlier non-binding Letter of Intent, the form of Seller Note and a distractor email thread on transition logistics. Three issues are planted. First, the APA's definition of Assumed Liabilities sweeps in pre-closing product liability, which the LOI had left with the Seller, and Muvux's indemnity for Assumed Liabilities is carved out of every cap. Second, the Seller Note makes a change of control of Muvux's parent an Event of Default unless the Holder consents. The APA itself discloses the parent's pending merger, and no consent is obtained. Third, the Seller Note overrides the APA's carve-out of Excluded Liabilities from the seller indemnity cap, and the APA's precedence clause lets the Note control.

issues.label: Uncapped buyer indemnity for pre-closing product liability
issues.description: Section 1.3(c) of the APA (D1) defines Assumed Liabilities to include all product liability claims relating to the Products, whether manufactured or sold before or after the Closing. Section 9.3(b) obliges Buyer to indemnify Seller for all Losses arising from Assumed Liabilities. Section 9.5(c) provides that no cap, basket or other limitation applies to claims under Section 9.3(b). Read together, these provisions leave Muvux with unlimited exposure for implant failure and recall claims on devices Pisen made and sold before Closing. For an orthopedic implant line that is potentially the largest liability in the deal. It also departs from Paragraph 4 of the LOI (D2), under which pre-closing product liability stays with Seller as an Excluded Liability. The APA supersedes the LOI under Section 11.9, so the LOI does not cure the point.
detect_terms: whether manufactured or sold before or after the Closing
issues.expected_finding: Under APA Sections 1.3(c), 9.3(b) and 9.5(c), Muvux assumes and must indemnify Seller, without any cap, for product liability on implants Pisen sold before Closing, contrary to the LOI's allocation of that liability to Seller. The fix is to limit Assumed Liabilities to post-Closing sales and move pre-closing product liability into Excluded Liabilities.

issues.label: Seller Note default triggered by parent's pending merger
issues.description: Section 6(e) of the form Seller Note (D3) makes it an Event of Default if Maker, or any Person that directly or indirectly controls Maker, undergoes a Change of Control without the Holder's prior written consent. Section 7 provides that on an Event of Default the Holder may declare the full $14,000,000 principal immediately due, with default interest at 4% above the Note rate. Section 5.5 of the APA (D1) discloses that Muvux's parent, Muvux Orthopedics Holdings, Inc., entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated August 27, 2026 with Ardentis Surgical Partners, L.P. That merger would be a Change of Control of an entity controlling Maker. Neither the APA nor the Note includes Pisen's consent or a carve-out for that transaction. Completing the parent merger would therefore let Pisen accelerate the Note.
detect_terms: any Person that directly or indirectly controls Maker
without the prior written consent of Holder
issues.expected_finding: The Seller Note's change-of-control default in Section 6(e) is triggered by the parent's August 27, 2026 merger with Ardentis disclosed in APA Section 5.5, and the Holder's consent has not been obtained. Muvux faces acceleration of the $14,000,000 Note plus default interest, so it should obtain Pisen's written consent or carve the parent merger out of the definition of Change of Control before the Note is issued.

issues.label: Seller Note subjects Excluded Liabilities claims to the seller cap
issues.description: Section 9.5(b) of the APA (D1) excludes from the $8,160,000 Seller Indemnity Cap any claims under Section 9.2(c) for Excluded Liabilities, which include pre-closing taxes, environmental liabilities and remediation of Seller's FDA warning letter. Section 8(b) of the form Seller Note (D3) states that, notwithstanding Section 9.5(b) of the Purchase Agreement, Holder's aggregate liability for all claims under Section 9.2, including claims under Section 9.2(c) for Excluded Liabilities, shall not exceed the Seller Indemnity Cap. Only Fraud remains outside the cap. Section 11.9 of the APA says the Seller Note controls over the APA in any conflict, so the Note's narrower carve-out governs. Muvux's recovery for Excluded Liabilities it never agreed to assume is therefore capped at 12% of the price.
detect_terms: including claims under Section 9.2(c) for Excluded Liabilities
shall not exceed the Seller Indemnity Cap
issues.expected_finding: Because APA Section 11.9 gives the Seller Note precedence, Note Section 8(b) overrides the APA Section 9.5(b) carve-out and caps Muvux's recovery for Excluded Liabilities at $8,160,000. Section 8(b) should be deleted or conformed so that Excluded Liabilities claims remain uncapped, and the precedence clause should be revised so the APA controls on indemnification.
